title: Parity-Time Symmetry of Plasma Waves
abstract: The susceptibility tensor of a homogeneous collisionless magnetized plasma possesses parity-time (PT) symmetry. For a stationary gyrotropic equilibrium, with the wave vector $\mathbf{k}$ and the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ in the $x$--$z$ plane, the kinetic response satisfies $χ(ω^*,\mathbf{k})=Rχ(ω,\mathbf{k})^*R$, where $R=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$. We show that the susceptibility PT-symmetry is a reduced-response-space manifestation of PT symmetry of the underpinning kinetic system. We identify parity $P$ and time reversal $T$ on the electromagnetic kinetic eigenmode space and show that the Hamiltonian operator $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{VM}}$ of the linearized Vlasov--Maxwell system is PT-symmetric, satisfying $PT\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{VM}}(PT)^{-1}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{VM}}$. The PT symmetry of the homogeneous magnetized Vlasov--Poisson eigenproblem is also established. Many kinetic instabilities associated with nonmonotonic distributions, rings, loss cones, and resonant energetic-particle populations are fundamentally spontaneous PT-symmetry breaking, which is achieved through and only through Krein collisions. Three examples demonstrate distinct utilities of this analysis. Definite-sign cyclotron residues protect thermal Bernstein modes from spontaneous PT-symmetry breaking. The nonmonotonic Dory--Guest--Harris distribution permits sign-indefinite residues and Krein collisions, for which we derive an analytical instability threshold and growth rate. The recently discovered mode-pole resonance instability provides a distinct realization of spontaneous PT-symmetry breaking and illustrates how PT symmetry can guide the discovery of kinetic instabilities with applications to fusion energy. These results establish PT symmetry as a structural principle of plasma waves and instabilities and open new directions for studying spectral topology in kinetic plasmas.
summary: This work establishes PT symmetry as a fundamental structural principle governing plasma waves in magnetized, collisionless plasmas. By proving that the underlying kinetic Hamiltonian is PT-symmetric, the authors link spontaneous symmetry breaking to the onset of kinetic instabilities. This framework offers new tools for predicting plasma instabilities and understanding spectral topology.
main_problem: The paper investigates the parity-time (PT) symmetry of the susceptibility tensor and the underlying kinetic system in a homogeneous, collisionless, magnetized plasma.
main_result: The susceptibility exhibits PT symmetry, which is shown to be a reduced-response-space manifestation of the full Vlasov–Maxwell Hamiltonian being PT-symmetric. Spontaneous PT-symmetry breaking is fundamentally linked to kinetic instabilities occurring via Krein collisions.
method: The analysis involves identifying parity (P) and time reversal (T) operators on the electromagnetic kinetic eigenmode space and applying the framework of PT-symmetric quantum mechanics to plasma response functions.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous collisionless magnetized plasma with a stationary gyrotropic equilibrium. The theory is built upon the linearized Vlasov–Maxwell and Vlasov–Poisson systems.
key_observables: Susceptibility tensor $\chi(\omega, \mathbf{k})$, eigenfrequencies ($\omega$), and the Hamiltonian operator $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{VM}}$.
important_parameters: Plasma frequency ($\omega_{ps}$), cyclotron frequency ($\Omega_s$), and the wave vector $\mathbf{k}$.
main_assumptions: The plasma is assumed to be collisionless, and the equilibrium is stationary and gyrotropic.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometry of the wave vector and the reflection operator $R$. Other figures schematically show the movement of eigenfrequencies across the real axis during explicit PT-symmetry breaking.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the PT symmetry of the susceptibility tensor $\chi$ (Section III), and then extends this analysis to prove the PT symmetry of the full Hamiltonian operator $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{VM}}$ of the Vlasov–Maxwell system (Section IV).
why_interesting: The application of PT-symmetry concepts, typically from quantum mechanics, to classical plasma wave dynamics provides a powerful structural principle for understanding stability and spectral topology in complex, non-Hermitian physical systems.

FIG. 4. Schematic destabilization by explicit PT-symmetry breaking, following the concept illustrated in Refs. 16 and 17. The open circle marks the initial real eigenfrequency of the mode that becomes unstable. The arrow shows its motion into the upper half-plane as an explicit PT symmetry break- ing perturbation of strength ϵ increases. Filled circles mark the frequencies of the perturbed operator Hϵ; the other three modes remain on the real axis. No Krein collision is required, and the frequencies need not form complex-conjugate pairs. Colors identify branches, and the axes have arbitrary scales.
